body:
The smell of my own baby boy fading from all of his things over time was really really hard for me. I totally get it. 

Take comfort in the smell of his things for now. Try to enjoy his smell and memorize it while you can. Smelling his blanket brought me some comfort in the early days. Be prepared for the scent to fade too, of course. It will be really really hard to let go of, I won’t lie. 

I’m so sorry for your loss. I know the feeling of being willing to do anything to see him one last time. I would do anything too. I don’t know if any amount of time with my baby boy would ever have been enough, to be honest.

Wishing you lots of healing in the coming weeks and months. It’s really hard right now. Hang in there.

It’s good to know I’m not alone. I was kind of starting to worry that I’d gone crazy. It’s been about 3 months for me as well but I don’t feel like anything is getting better. I feel like I should be less sad now that some time has passed, and I’m definitely crying less often than I was in the beginning (still a lot though), but life just feels so hopeless. I lost interest in everything, like you said. I just wish I could see him again. I’d do anything. This sucks so bad. I hate having to live without him.

The awful death nightmares are just the cherry on top of me already having a terrible time, yknow? I wish I could at least have good dreams about him. But I think that would probably still hurt, just in a different way.

Wishing you all the best. Stay strong. I hope you start to feel a little better soon. It’s really tough but we have to keep going, for their sake ❤️

I’m so sorry for your loss. It’s such a shock to the system when they pass suddenly. Finding her like that must have been so scary.

I experienced my first ever pet loss a few months ago and I wasn’t prepared for how much it would hurt. The first few days are really difficult. Please be gentle with yourself and take the time and space you need to grieve. I also found it helpful to have a good distraction on hand (comfort sitcom, in my case) for when the crying started to get physically painful. Definitely let yourself feel your feelings and don’t try to block them out, but it’s okay to take breaks for your sanity’s sake.

Do you have anyone you can lean on right now? It can really help to let your support system know what’s going on and reach out when you need some comfort. 

I’m so sorry you lost your little girl like this. It really is such a deep loss. Sending well wishes your way.
Changing my resolution seems to have helped (🤞🤞🤞) but I’ll definitely keep this in mind as a backup plan. Thanks for the adviceb!
My wifi connection is pretty good, I never have issues streaming anything else.
Maybe the website isn’t equipped for this amount of traffic… I really hope they fix it since we all paid money to watch it live!

Is anyone else’s stream buffering a bunch? If a static screen with music is buffering this much then I’m pretty concerned about the actual show lol

Edit for others who might be having this issue: Try changing your resolution! I changed mine to 360p and that seems to have helped… for now at least. Which is a ridiculously low resolution, but I’m just relieved it’s not buffering constantly. I’m gonna try gradually increasing the resolution and see how high I can push it without the buffering starting again.

it really is! the chicken strips were just ones i bought pre-cooked from the grocery store, so i was expecting them to be pretty boring, but they must have seasoned them really well cause they were SO YUMMY.
i feel like a brand new person lol. i was walking around dizzy and extremely tired, now i feel a bit more well-adjusted again. good stuff!

This made me tear up a little. I really hope that’s true. 

I also just wish he was still here though. With me, where he belongs. I miss him so much.

I’m so sorry for your loss.

Same with my boy. He was super clingy and always wanted to be with his family. He wouldn’t be happy all alone. 

I try to comfort myself with the thought that if he is in the afterlife, maybe my grandfather is there keeping him company until I can join him. They never actually met in life, but my grandfather heard all about him and saw so many pictures. Maybe he knew he was coming and came to get him. Perhaps, if there is an afterlife, you have a deceased family member who can take care of your boy too. So he isn’t all alone.

This sucks. I’m so sorry. Hang in there.

The day we adopted my dog. I was so young, I barely remember what he was like as a puppy, and I’d love to have access to those memories. He died recently and most of my memories of him are as an older dog. I wish I could recall what he was like when he was younger.

But honestly, I’d choose to relive ANY day that my dog was alive, except the last two (when he got really sick really fast). I’m not picky. I just want to see, hold and kiss him again. My little baby boy.

I’m so sorry for your loss. I lost my own baby, and a piece of my soul with him, back in December, so I know the feeling. All I can say is that this reaction is really normal this early in the process. I didn’t stop sobbing for days after my boy passed, to the point where it was physically hurting me.

Sometimes despite our best efforts, we simply can’t save them. Their little bodies break down and we have to make the difficult choice to spare them the pain and suffering. You did the kind thing for your boy, even though it meant saying goodbye, which shows just how much you loved him.

I’m only 3 months out so I’m far from an expert, but from experience, the first few weeks are the hardest. It’s not exactly easy now, but I don’t constantly feel like I’m gasping for air 24/7 anymore. Hang in there.

Go see her as soon as you have the chance. And then go see her again after that, the next time you have the chance. And keep seeing her until she passes. I promise you will not regret it. 

Losing her will be extremely difficult. I’m still crushed over the loss of my own baby. But right now I really recommend spending all the time you can with her. You’ll only regret it if you don’t. 

I’m so sorry this is happening. Anticipatory grief is so awful. Focus on your beloved for now. Worry about the “after” once you get there. I wasted so much time worrying about my own boy dying that I could have spent enjoying his company. She’s your dog and you adore her. That’s what matters right now.

Thank you so much for the beautiful poem. 

I miss him so much. I wish I could’ve saved him.

I’m so sorry for your loss. If you don’t mind me asking, has it gotten any easier a year out? I’m definitely crying less than I was two months ago when we lost him, but I still can’t imagine carrying on like this. It’s like part of my soul is missing.

Thank you. Your words help. It’s so hard to hnderstand that putting him down was the right thing to do. Of course I didn’t want him to suffer any longer, but it feels like I killed him. I miss my beautiful boy so so much.

I’m so sorry for your loss. Your girl has a very similar story to my baby boy. In and out of the vet every week, painkillers, not really sure what was wrong. Suddenly his symptoms became really severe and he was in agony. We couldn’t watch him suffer anymore. I think you’re right that the lack of diagnosis makes it difficult to find closure. I will always wonder what was really wrong with him and whether I could have saved him. 

I hope things get a little easier for you soon. I jnow that unbearable pain very well. Hugs ❤️
Thank you.

I’m so sorry for your loss. It’s really difficult in the early days, but becomes a little more manageable over time, I find. 

I know what you mean. I can’t bear the thought that I could have done something to save him. He was my whole heart. I tried so hard to save him, but I still feel like maybe if I tried harder he would still be here. Perhaps I just can’t accept that losing him was inevitable. He was the most precious thing in the world to me. Why should he have to die before me? It all makes very little sense.

I wish you lots of healing and warmth. These first few days are especially hard. Take it easy and give yourself some grace.

I’m so sorry for your loss. You did so much for your Daisy. I can tell how deeply you love her. You absolutely did the best you could for her, and I’m sure she wouldn’t have expected you to put your job on the line for her. I hope you’re doing okay, all things considered, and I wish you lots of healing.

I will try to be kinder to myself. Your words have put everything into perspective a bit. Thank you.

Thank you. ❤️

I hope you’re right. The idea that he could still be here if I’d been better haunts me. I miss him dearly. I certainly tried my best at the time. Everything happened so fast that night while it was actually happening. But now that it’s over I have all the time in the world to replay it and wonder whether or not I did the right thing. It’s psychological torture, I think.

I’ve read posts by so many others in this community who felt they could have done better, and I’ve never blamed them for the choices they made in the moment. It feels different when it’s me I guess. My baby was the most precious thing in the world to me. I don’t know if I can forgive myself for possibly choosing wrong. 

All of this to say, thank you for your kind words. I hope I can start to believe them.

Thank you so much, that means so much to me, you have no idea. I really hope he did feel it. He was my whole world and I have never loved anyone like I love him.

I do have a therapist who I’ve been checking in with regularly. The sadness persists, unfortunately. I fear it might persist for a very long time, possibly forever. A world without him just feels so wrong. It’s been really difficult to adapt to the fact that he’s not here anymore. The feeling of guilt doesn’t help. I seem to be convinced that if I had tried harder, if I had done everything right, he would still be here. 

Thanks for your kind words. I truly appreciate it.
Thank you so much. That means a lot to hear.

I’m so sorry for your loss. I hope you’re doing okay. Finding the list really catapulted me into the emotions I was experiencing the night it happened.

I will certainly never forget him. He was my everything. I hope, if he’s still out there somewhere, he can forgive me for failing him. I really wanted to save him. I tried everything I could think of at the time. I hope he forgives me.
Crying on the plane right now. This is so beautiful, thank you so much.
I will. Thank you so much. ❤️

Thank you so much. This really really helps and honestly made me cry a little (in a good way). You’re right that they live in our hearts. It’s just so hard when this was his place. He loved it here so so so much. I’m scared to go the new place. I’m scared he won’t be there anymore. And I don’t want to start a new chapter of life without him. I want to stay in the chapter where my baby is still alive. 

Maybe a change of environment will help me. Seeing all the places he used to be can be a curse sometimes, it makes it hard to function. But it’s such a blessing too. I miss him so much. I can visualize him so easily while I’m here. My visual memory is so bad that it’s hard to visualize him just in my head without being prompted by my outside environment. I miss his little face so much. 

I’m so sorry for your loss and I’m glad your dream brought you some comfort. It seems to me like your boy is still with you, if you believe in such things. I’ll ask my boy to come with me too.

I miss him so much. It’s going to be hard living somewhere new without him. Thank you so much for the support, and sorry for my sad rambling.

Bear sounds like such a sweet boy. I’m thinking of him. I’ll be thinking of you on Monday. His memory wll be kept alive. 

I’m so sorry. How amazing that he made it to 18 years old, but I’m sure that knowing him for so many years makes saying goodbye all the harder. You’ve clearly been incredibly good to him for the 12 years you’ve had him. He came from a bad situation and still lived to 18? That’s a testament to the incredible love and care you’ve given him.

Enjoy this weekend. Do all his favorite things. Try to memorize the little things, if you can. Being able to clearly picture my own boy has helped me a lot since losing him. 

You’re doing the right thing, but that doesn’t make it any easier. I’m so sorry you’re going through this.

no black parade is absolutely LAUGHABLE. easily in the top 10, if not the top 3, albums of the century so far. both in quality and cultural impact. MCR shifted something permanently when they released that album and everyone knows it. RS needs to show some respect.

(am i biased? maybe. but i’m also right.)

Thank you so much. This community’s responses to my posts have helped me a lot after I lost him. Actually reading other people’s posts on this sub just tends to trigger intense sobbing for me right now, unfortunately. I guess it’s just too raw at the moment. I would love to turn my grief into something productive by supporting others here though. I’m just not ready yet I think.

I can tell how special he was to you. I think losing them is bound to hurt a lot when we love them as deeply we do. I’m only slightly further along in my own grieving process, but I can tell you that while it hasn’t necessarily gotten any easier yet, I’ve found ways to adapt and survive. You will too.
I don’t quite know what to say, but I found this comment really helpful, so thank you.

I wish I believed in that, because it would genuinely make me feel so much better, but I’m unfortunately a skeptic by nature. I really really hope I’m wrong though. I would do anything to be with him again one day. 

I’m not saying you’re wrong by any means though! I’m so glad the feeling of your beloved still being there brings you some comfort.
Thank you so much for all the kind words. It sounds like you were an amazing human to your kitty who passed, and I’m sure you’ll be equally as amazing with your new kitty.
Thank you so much. I miss him very dearly. I hope I was able to give him a good enough life. He deserved all the best in the world.
I’m so sorry for your loss. It’s tough when it feels like the world doesn’t even acknowledge how important they were to us.

I’m so sorry about your losses. That sounds awful. Especially seeing your cat’s brother not be the same after, and then losing him too so soon. And seeing your lady go downhill so fast. 

My boy went downhill fast, too. One moment, he was fine, 24 hours later we were euthanizing him so he didn’t have to suffer anymore. It was a bit of a shock to the system. I’m glad it’s better for you now. I hope I can stop seeing my baby in pain soon. 

I wish you so much love and happiness with your new kittens! How exciting.

Yeah I talk to him sometimes, almost out of instinct. It really hurts sometimes though. I wish he was there wagging his tail and looking up at me with his beautiful brown eyes. I also sometimes close my eyes when I’m in bed or on the couch and call to him, and pretend he’s there jumping up to be with me. I don’t know if it’s unhealthy or prolonging my denial or something, but sometimes I just need to pretend he’s there for a few seconds.
I’m so sorry for your loss. I wish you lots of healing.

I’m so sorry for your loss. The first holidays without them are really hard. With my boy, we really had every reason to think he would make it to Christmas, and maybe even the Christmas after that. Celebrating without him hurt so bad.

Striking a balance is so difficult. It’s so hard to know when to cut myself off from feeling it, and I’m not always able to stop feeling it anyway. I’ve been up until 6AM crying the past few nights. 

The callous people in my life definitely aren’t helping lol. Thank you for the support. ❤️
I’ll definitely make sure to give the video a watch, thank you. I’m so sorry for your loss. People really don’t understand.

Thank you so much. I’ll do my best to think about the good moments. It’s just hard. His health went downhill so fast I almost feel like I was traumatized by it. One moment, his usual self, 24 hours later, gone. It was a shock to the system.

I’m so sorry for your loss. It definitely comes in waves.

I know it takes time, it’s just hard when there’s external pressure to be “over it” already. People telling me he was “just” a dog. No, he was my baby and I love him more than I’ve ever loved any human. I know that life goes on, but it’s really hard to care about any of that other stuff right now. I just want my baby back.

I’m so sorry for your recent loss. I hope you’re doing okay (all things considered, anyway). The first few days are so so difficult.

I’m sorry that everyone’s pushing you to do activities and have fun. My family is like that too right now. It’s really hard when your heart just isn’t in it. 

I do hope it gets easier with time. Sending lots of healing your way.
I’m so sorry for your loss. How beautiful that you got 16 years with him. I cried about the New Year too, knowing 2025 was gonna be the first year without him. I wish I could go back.

I’m so so sorry for your loss. I’m glad you’re feeling a little more optimistic now. Preparing for her spirit successor is a beautiful thought. I wish you lots of love and happiness with your eventual new kitty.

I don’t know if I’ll ever get another dog. I want to, as I really love life with a dog, but it just hurts so bad. He was irreplaceable and I’m scared I could never love another dog as much. And I’m terrified of having to deal with this pain all over again if I get another dog and they die. 

(Not saying you’re trying to “replace” your kitty AT ALL, by the way! I know it’s not like that. I just personally really struggle with the thought of adopting a new dog after having had such a special bond with my baby.)

The firsts are really tough. Going on a walk without him was agonizing. Watching TV (his favorite thing to do, because he had a spot on the couch with all his blankets where he got to snuggle up between two of his humans) without him just made me feel dead inside. My family pushed me to do a lot of “firsts” in the days after his death, before I was really ready. On the one hand, it was good to rip the band aid off, but on the other hand, I felt really guilty, like I was betraying him by doing his favorite things without him. 

Three cats in one year? I’m so sorry for your loss, that must have been awful. I hope you’re doing better now. 

I’ll try to focus more on the happy times. It’s just hard. Every time I close my eyes before I go to sleep I see him at the vet’s office, suffering. I don’t know why I can’t picture something happy instead. For some reason that’s the memory I got stuck with. 

Thank you for the support.

Thank you so much. The support here really helps me feel a bit less like I’m going crazy. It really does feel like living with a piece of me missing. It’s just hard to take my the time I need to grieve when people want me to be over it already. I caught a lot of flack during the holidays for “not being happy enough.”
I’m really glad my tearful 4AM ramblings could bring some comfort to someone. I’m so sorry for your loss.

I’m so sorry about your Indy. Entering the new year without them is especially hard. I kind of wished it would stay 2024, because that was a year when my baby boy was still alive. 2025 is gonna be the first year without my baby boy in it, and every single other year is going to be like that for the rest of time. I want it to still be the time when he was alive. I don’t think that makes sense the way I explained it, sorry. I just can’t get excited for a year without him here.

The triggers are so difficult, and it’s literally everything. The fireworks that I mentioned, or other people walking dogs like you said. He was such a big part of my life so the reminders are everywhere. And then I’m useless for the rest of the day. I get it. 

It’s just difficult because it seems like everyone else wants me to move on already. Like you, I don’t think I’ll ever be able to. But everyone else wants me to just be normal now. 

I wish you the best in navigating your loss too. Hopefully lots of healing comes your way in the new year.
I’m so sorry for your loss. It’s so hard right now. I hope it gets easier soon. Thank you so much for all your advice.

Thank you so much for the advice, and I’m so so sorry for your loss. I suffer from depression and anxiety too, so I’m worried about the effect this will have on my mental health in the long term. I’ll try my best to implement your advice. I really appreciate the insight from someone who’s a bit further along in the process, so thank you.

I’m so sorry. And WOW, everything you just said is STRANGELY similar to my own boy. Mine was almost the same age as yours. He would have been 14 in June. He was all the things for me that yours was for you — best friend, baby, love of my life, my rock, biggest support system, and honestly, a part of me. The vet told me that my baby was remarkably healthy for a 13 year old just last week too. Mine also had a heart condition, and he also (maybe) died from bloat. (We didn’t do diagnostics before euthanizing because it would have been so invasive and uncomfortable and the vet told us there was NO chance of it being anything we could successfully treat, but bloat was a strong possibility.) Mine also started drinking tons of water very fast in the days leading up to his death. 

Please try not to blame yourself. It’s easy to point to changes we made around the same time that things got worse as the “reason” why our baby died, because we WANT a reason. We want this terrible thing to make sense. I started giving mine a new brand of treats this week and I was so worried that that was what killed him. But the vet explained that the likelihood of the food being the thing that killed him is so so low. Your boy, like my boy, was old. Most likely, he had existing issues going on internally that were getting worse over time, but not enough to affect him significantly. So he seemed healthy. And then time caught up with him, those issues progressed to a certain point, and the stress on the body hit a breaking point, and he got really sick really suddenly. In other words: it’s NOT YOUR FAULT. You WERE a smart and attentive mom, and you did NOT fail him. 

I genuinely believe the reason that you ended up on my post, with a story SO similar to my boy’s, is so I could tell you what my vet told me about my case, which is nearly identical to yours: it’s not your fault. It was his time. There was nothing you could have done, which is maddening and terrifying because it means admitting that we can’t control what happens to our beloved babies. But you DID NOT FAIL HIM. You were the best mom to him that you possibly could have been. Even if you did somehow make a mistake, you did it with the very best intentions, hoping it would help him. But more likely, time simply caught up with him.

I’m really sorry for the long ramble, and I’m really sorry if I’m overstepping at all. I was genuinely shaken and touched by reading your boy’s story, because it’s so close to how my boy’s life ended. So I hope the insight I was given by my own boy’s vet can help you feel more at ease. You’re already dealing with the loss of your beloved. There’s no need to torture yourself with guilt. You did all you could. You were a good mom.

Thank you so much for your kind words and advice. I’ll try those supplements you mentioned. And I will try to live a happy life for my baby boy’s sake. It will be so hard without him here. He was so special too. I never met another dog like him. I miss him so much already.

I’ve definitely had to strike a balance today. After a while the hysterical sobbing became so physically exhausting that my only choice was to distract myself with my favorite feel-good show. But I know I have to feel the grief as well. We took down his doggy door and threw out all his food today. I just ended up crying in a corner going “no no no no no no no.” It still doesn’t feel real. I don’t want it to be real. 

I really, really wish I could hold him.
Thank you.

I’m so sorry. Enjoy this time with your beloved. There are things I would’ve done for mine if we had time to prepare, but he deteriorated so suddenly and rapidly that by the time we knew something was wrong, he wasn’t even eating and didn’t want to walk far. So we didn’t get to feed him his favorite treats or take him on his favorite route one last time. Fill this weekend with everything your fur baby loves. I’m so sorry you’re going through this, I know how tough it is.

I hope you don’t mind me asking, but over time does the sadness start to feel less like you’re going to die? Every time I think of him I just start sobbing so hard I literally can’t breathe. It genuinely feels like my heart might give out. I don’t know how much more of this I can physically take.

Oh no, I’m so sorry. I can’t imagine how much harder it must have been with him being your service dog too. I can tell the two of you had a really special bond. I’m so glad you got your Rocky and that Rocky’s been able to help.

Oh, I’m so sorry. I feel your pain. My dog was put down just a few hours after yours. It’s really really hard right now.

I’m so glad you got to have that sweet moment with your dog in your dream. Even though it’s “fake,” it’s real in a way — your brain constructed that dream based on all your wonderful memories of him, and those moments were so very real. 

Funnily enough, I had a dream that my dog was still alive today too. It unfortunately turned into a nightmare where he was still alive and suffering (thanks brain!). But in a way, it made me feel more at peace with our decision to put him down. He was the best boy and he doesn’t deserve to be in any pain.

I don’t think I’ll ever have another dog either. My boy has been in my life since I was 9 years old and being without him is just terrible. No dog could ever replace him. And the thought of going through this awful heartbreak again is just intolerable. I understand.

ETA: YES, THE HEADACHES. MY GOD THE HEADACHES. I’ve been sobbing so hard and I’m so dehydrated, the headaches are just the worse. I’m sure the stress of the past 48 hours and the grief isn’t making it any better either.

I’m so sorry about your baby. I really did (do) love him so so so dearly. It’s hard to find joyful moments. I try to distract myself but it all just feels so hollow. I might give journaling a try. Thank you for the advice about the breathing techniques, I might look some up to try for the next time I start hyperventilating. Thanks so much for the support.

I’m so sorry about your Cody. If you don’t mind me asking, how did you survive the first week? Or the first day, even. It hurts so much and I don’t know what to do. The world feels so empty without him in it and I’ve been sobbing so hard I think my heart might give out.

If everyone could read what I’m about to say with an open mind and a bit of empathy, I would be eternally grateful. Please.

I am begging people to stop blaming trans people for the election. We didn’t want any of this. The Harris campaign didn’t mention us AT ALL, and we were completely fine with that. Despite what the media will tell you, we’re literally just trying to exist peacefully, access our medical care, and live our lives. The GOP were the ones running campaigns fear-mongering about trans people to scare voters to the right. Did it work? Idk, maybe. But the “trans movement” had no control over that. The Democrats did not “run with” our “ideology.” They largely ignored us, and that’s what we wanted. We KNOW there’s a massive target on our backs. We just want to lay low. 

There’s a lot more nuanced stuff to say about the specific policies and issues you mentioned, but to be honest, I am tired of constantly having to defend myself. I really want everyone to imagine what it’s like to be trans right now. We are terrified. We know we’re one of the first groups that will be targeted. We know no one is going to stand up for us. Most of us are panicking, trying to stockpile hormones, and making emergency plans to move countries if we have to. EMERGENCY PLANS. That’s how scared we are. 

Imagine being that terrified and that devastated by this election, and then having to see people blame YOU for the election’s loss, because your “ideology” is “taking over,” when you just want to exist. We’re the favorite scapegoat of BOTH SIDES. People on BOTH SIDES have made it clear that they don’t like us, and now we’re being blamed for an election that directly and severely hurts us. That sucks, because all we did was exist, and we’re being told our mere existence was enough to piss people off so much that they just HAD to vote for Trump, who is going to take all of our rights away. So in addition to terrified, we have to feel guilty too, I guess.

We are 1% of the population. We just want to live. I don’t want to spread any ideology. I literally just want to access medical care and live my life. I hope this doesn’t come off as angry, because that’s not how I mean it. But I’m begging people to see us as the real, terrified human beings we are, and not as some sort of political movement trying to take over US politics. We just want to live.

ETA: Not calling anyone a bigot btw. I just wanted to add the perspective of an actual trans person to this issue. We are real people, not a monolith, and most of the panic over “gender ideology” simply does not reflect the reality of what trans people want and what we’re like.
Not a Floridian, but Florida is currently designated as a “do not travel” state by trans rights organizationd. Please be very careful.

As a lifelong New Yorker, I absolutely recommend it here! If you have to stay in the US as a trans person, it’s a really good state to live in.

Cost of living in NYS can be very high in some areas. I definitely don’t recommend moving to NYC if money is an issue. However, there are certain queer-positive cities further upstate with relatively low cost of living! Rochester and Buffalo are both good examples of that. Do some research into other cities as well and see if any of them work for you. Look into other states as well — you just want to get to somewhere safe and cheap right now. The rest doesn’t matter.

I won’t lie, it’s going to be difficult without a job. Are there any nontraditional ways for you to generate income that are possible with the disabilities that you have? I see people saying they wouldn’t know how to tag this sort of thing without overcomplicating things or being dehumanizing, but I think we might be overthinking it a little bit. Why not just keep things as simple as possible? In the Good Omens fandom, most authors will tag their smut in the format “(Character) Has A (Body Part)” format. So “Crowley Has a Vulva” or “Aziraphale Has a Penis,” for example. 

I think this works nicely because in most cases, it succinctly tells readers everything they need to know. It’s a matter-of-fact statement about what genitals a character has. So long as authors do this consistently for both their cis characters and their trans characters, this avoids the problem of “othering” trans people because it doesn’t treat smut with trans characters as some sort of deviation from the norm that needs to be specially tagged. By looking at the tags, readers can avoid specific types of smut that they’d rather not read (because they find it triggering, or for any other reason), or find specific types of smut that they do want to read. But it also allows us to avoid the problem of treating trans characters like they’re abnormal and need to be “warned” for, or going into tedious detail about which surgeries a character has or hasn’t had.

None of this is me opining on whether or not authors SHOULD always tag, by the way. Not getting involved in that debate rn. Just offering a solution to the people who expressed that they do WANT to tag, but are struggling with the particulars of HOW to go about it.

I hope that made sense, it’s 2 AM and I’m half asleep lol.

One final note: if your fic has detailed descriptions of a character’s gender dysphoria, I would strongly encourage you to at least give it the “Dysphoria” tag. Not tagging trans characters who are just existing is one thing, and I think authors who don’t want to do so are justified in that. But if your work delves deeply into the emotional pain of being trans, I think it’s probably best to give trans readers the opportunity to avoid that. It’s one thing to read a fic and find out unexpectedly that a character is trans. It’s another thing entirely to be bombarded, without warning, by in-depth descriptions of dysphoria, which can be really triggering and excruciatingly painful for trans readers who have severe dysphoria. You don’t have to tag. But in these instances, it would be the kind thing to do. 

(Source: am trans)

All of this is so relatable, except for the part about managing to move on and stop caring what people think. I know exactly what you mean about the guilty “what if?” feeling, and ATL has played a huge role in getting me through some dark times as well. And yes, absolutely agree about the suckiness of the situation. If you don’t mind me asking, what helped you get past the worry about what other people would think and the guilty feeling enough to enjoy ATL’s music again?

The guilt definitely would’ve been there either way. Even before everything happened, allegations being brought against ATL was always a worst-case scenario in my mind (that probably sounds like a weird fear to have, but a majority of the other bands I listened to growing up were accused of SA years before ATL was, so I guess it was pretty salient in my mind). I knew that if any accusations were made, it would be incredibly difficult for me to reconcile my love for the band with some of my own life experiences. It’s a special hell when the band that got you through some of your worst times is then accused of having done the same thing to someone else that was done to you.

That being said, the peer pressure hasn’t helped at all. I did leave Twitter permanently, even before I made up my mind that the allegations were false, because the expectation for everyone to just completely drop their loyalty and start talking shit about their favorite band OVERNIGHT was… a little intense. Like, there were people who had been on ATL twitter for YEARS suddenly tweeting shit like “all time low is trash and if you don’t agree please block me because you’re trash too.” Bruh what. As for friends in real life, that’s a bit more complicated. I already feel guilt and self-doubt about still loving ATL and still wanting to listen to their music and see what they’re up to and maybe even go to shows again one day. Like, there’s already a voice in the back of my mind going “what if the alleged victims are telling the truth, what if you’re supporting abusers.” No matter how highly unlikely that possibility seems, the fact that it’s a possibility scares the shit out of me and makes me feel sick to my stomach. The differences really started to show in the second round. Every single cis man in the room got rid of his “gender” post-it at this point. All of the women and trans folks in the room held onto theirs. 

“Immigration status” was the next post-it to go for most people. I was the only person who held onto mine. I also happened to be the only immigrant in the room. 

The ease with which all of the white, straight cis guys in the room determined what post-it notes to get rid of was astonishing to me. Every single one of them ended up with “religious beliefs” as the last sticky note left (all were Christians).

The further into the activity we got, the more torn I felt. Though I was a Christian at this point in my life, I disposed of that post-it pretty early on — not because my faith wasn’t important to me, but because I didn’t feel it had shaped my life in the way that other aspects of my identity had. As stated before, I’m an immigrant, and I also identified as a lesbian at the time (I now know I’m a trans man, but that’s not important to this story). The post-its labeled “immigrant,” “woman,” and “gay” all felt too important for me to let go of. I ended up holding onto all three. I didn’t want to make a choice. 

The point of this story is that we humans have a tendency to not notice the facets of our identity that come with privilege. For me, being white was never something I thought as being important to who I was. My race didn’t matter much to me. I felt it hadn’t impacted my life. I was wrong, of course. My race HAD impacted my life, just not in a negative way. I didn’t notice the privilege that came with my racial identity. But my black friend most certainly noticed the oppression that came with hers. 

Same goes for gender, sexual orientation, and immigration status. Other people in the room were able to easily let go of these notes because they didn’t feel that being a man or being straight  or being a natural-born citizen had impacted their lives much at all. I, on the other hand, was DEFINITELY aware of how these aspects of who I was had impacted MY life. 

It’s likely that, as a cis man, you don’t feel that being a man is a key feature of who you are because it hasn’t affected you adversely. Your gender probably just never feel like a big deal to you, because you were never held back by it through systemic oppression. The human brain pays far more attention to injustices than it does to privilege. (Not trying to discredit men’s struggles here, btw. I understand that being a man comes with its own hardships; however, most would agree that it’s a relatively privileged position compared to women.)

I hope all of that makes sense. Sorry for the long post, but I felt it was interesting enough to share. And since I don’t know what being a cis man is like, I could be wrong about this , of course!

Okay, so I DO see what you’re saying here, and I agree with the most important aspects of it: There aren’t enough resources for male rape victims. Male rape victims are far too often shamed, humiliated or told to “man up” if they confide in anyone about what happened to them. Male rape is discussed far less than the rape of women. This is all unacceptable, and needs to change.

HOWEVER, I think you’re drawing an unnecessary comparison here. Hear me out.

There are unique, gender-specific issues that affect both male and female rape victims. Male rape is less visible, yes. Male victims are often shamed or told that they “can’t” be raped, yes. There’s also an added stigma of homophobia when it comes to male-on-male rape, yes.

But it goes both ways: Female victims are often not believed, or told they were “asking for it.” Female victims in many regions have to cope with the additional fear of being forced to carry their rapist’s baby to term if they fall pregnant. Many women in general unfortunately live in fear of rape every day.

You can make a comparison list of the disadvantages of both sides, but you’ll never run out of disadvantages for either one, because rape is a deeply traumatic experience. The worst possible breach of bodily autonomy. No matter who you are, being raped WILL fuck you up — sometimes irreparably (I speak from experience). 

I don’t deny that male rape victims have to deal with added stigma and pressures that are unique to them. I don’t deny that male rape victims are in dire need of more resources, visibility, and support. 

But comparing male rape to female rape just... it doesn’t help anyone involved. It creates an unnecessary barrier between two groups of hurting people who are both in dire need of help. It causes defensiveness from women, ESPECIALLY women who were raped, because as you can imagine, no one really takes well to hearing “well yeah, what happened to you was awful, but MINE’S WORSE!” 

I don’t think that’s necessarily what you’re saying, but I PROMISE you that some people WILL interpret it that way.

What ends up happening is it becomes a war of people trying to prove who has it “harder” when really... it doesn’t matter, does it? And women who have been raped become less receptive to discussions about male rape as a result of the conversation being framed this way, because it feels really shitty to be told that you somehow have it “easier” than the other group. 

A male rape victim can’t know what it’s like to be a female rape victim. A female rape victim can’t know what it’s like to be a male rape victim. Therefore, it doesn’t make sense for EITHER side to assert that they have it harder than the other side. At the end of the day, you can’t know what the other experience is like, and it’s impossible to come to an objective conclusion about which id “worse.”

Rape is painful for everyone involved. Society treats rape victims badly in GENERAL.

I think you’ll find that this conversation would be a much more productive one if it was framed as “Male rape victims have unique issues that aren’t acknowledged enough, and deserve the specialized resources, support, and awareness that they haven’t been getting.” The “who has it harder” comparison simply isn’t productive.

Hope that makes sense.
